record.learning: When a scanner whitelists sidecar IO by declared runtime, keep every accepted runtime usable by allowing only its bounded stdio surface on the declared sidecar entrypoint.
evidence: CAS footgun-finder 019f3085-cb85-79d2-bfca-c64bf241abfe found Deno was accepted by validateSidecarCommand but Deno stdio was unconditionally rejected; bun test and bun run proof passed after harness/pack-utils.mjs and test/adapter_self_containment.test.mjs fix.
record.application: For future sidecar runtime changes, update runtime validation, self-containment allowlists, docs, and entrypoint-bound regressions together.

record.learning: When a capability adapter duplicates manifest policy fields, prefer a verifier parity check that requires adapter manifest() to expose and match the full enforced policy surface, including secrets, because otherwise verified packs can drift and reject callers that followed the published manifest.
evidence: Post-fix footgun CAS 019f30b2-1490-7541-a184-70342b36639d found verified packs could still drift between manifest and adapter policy fields; verifyPack parity checks plus adapter secretRequirements exposure fixed it with bun test and bun run proof passing.
record.application: For future pack policy changes, update adapter manifest(), manifest.json, checksums, pack fingerprints, and verifier parity tests together before review-closeout.

record.learning: When a self-containment scanner accepts extensionless local imports, prefer covering every host runtime resolution candidate, including alternate executable extensions and JSON, because otherwise an uncovered sibling can be imported at runtime while checksums bless a different helper.
evidence: Standard CAS 019f30c0-7d51-7e43-9e25-3864fbe9bde4 found Bun could resolve helper.jsx or helper.mts outside the candidate list; adding .jsx/.mts/.cts/.json coverage plus regressions kept bun test and bun run proof passing.
record.application: For future import-resolution changes, validate candidate extensions against the runtime and add both uncovered-shadow and covered-helper tests before review-closeout.

record.learning: When adapter manifest() returns policy metadata that validation also reads, prefer returning a cloned or frozen manifest because otherwise caller mutation can alter later preflight or resolve policy decisions after verification.
evidence: Standard CAS 019f30cc-7f84-7761-8865-e62e456cfbda found packManifest arrays returned by manifest() were the same authority sets used by preEffectReason; structuredClone returns and an isolation regression fixed it with bun test and bun run proof passing.
record.application: For future adapter metadata changes, test that mutating manifest() output cannot change subsequent policy metadata before review-closeout.

record.learning: When a scanner expands an executable artifact predicate, prefer reusing that shared predicate in every downstream validator and adding false-positive tests, because duplicated regexes and broad heuristics can reject valid packs after the security fix.
evidence: Standard CAS 019f30f1-d3a8-7781-9d08-e3d312b1aa80 found sidecar entrypoint validation still omitted .jsx/.mts/.cts and computed-member detection rejected safe array literals; sharing EXECUTABLE_ARTIFACT and narrowing computed access kept bun test and bun run proof passing.
record.application: For future self-containment scanner changes, search for duplicated extension predicates and add at least one safe data-literal regression beside bypass regressions.

record.learning: When sidecar command validation derives an entrypoint from executable-looking arguments, prefer rejecting code-loading runtime flags before entrypoint selection because option payloads can masquerade as checksum-bound entrypoints while the real sidecar runs unchecked.
evidence: CAS invariant-ace rer_fab1e6be990e314500edb520b3545be30cc92846b32c221f1a4b8ef9d6f20de4 found bun --preload loader.jsx sidecar.mjs bypass; local repro printed BUG_REPRODUCED before fix; bun test and bun run proof passed after rejecting preload flags.
record.application: Keep sidecar runtime option parsing ahead of artifact/entrypoint binding and add regression coverage when adding executable extensions or runtime flags.

record.learning: When local import coverage handles directory specifiers, prefer modeling the runtime index resolution candidates because appending extensions to a trailing slash can bless shadow files while the runtime executes unchecked index modules.
evidence: Standard CAS rer_ece355acadb85ee6bc4f2d89b9e02e83fb2dc74e228b87ac8f467379476773b8 found import './helper/' could checksum helper/.js while Bun executes helper/index.js; local repro printed BUG_REPRODUCED before fix; bun test and bun run proof passed after covering index candidates.
record.application: For future import candidate changes, test trailing-slash directory imports alongside extensionless files and require coverage of runtime index targets.

record.learning: When supporting trailing-slash directory imports in a pack scanner, prefer rejecting package.json-backed directories unless package-main resolution is fully modeled because Bun can execute main/module targets before index fallbacks.
evidence: Standard CAS rer_a7c30d4084c3c72dbf896813c6a31bfed2ff9dd077459cc9b69fb276480ec751 found helper/package.json main could redirect ./helper/ to unchecked main.js; package-backed directory import repro now rejects; bun test and bun run proof passed.
record.application: For future directory import support, cover or reject package.json main/module/export paths explicitly instead of assuming index.* is sufficient.

record.learning: When hardening JavaScript self-containment scanner heuristics, treat review findings as an adversarial grammar corpus: replace broad regex matches with delimiter and context helpers, make Unicode identifiers and method/class/extends contexts first-class, and add both bypass and false-positive regressions before rerunning tuple-matched CAS.
evidence: CAS review findings in PR #1 exposed bypasses from regex/default/template braces, Unicode function and method names, word-operator divisions, private/bigint methods, and a quadratic comma scan in harness/pack-utils.mjs.
record.application: For future pack scanner changes, add targeted tests in test/adapter_self_containment.test.mjs for each grammar context, run bun proof, and reset the CAS clean streak after every scanner mutation.

record.learning: When a self-containment scanner uses broad computed-member regexes, run them on literal-stripped executable source because string and regex payload text such as object[key] or name[abc] is data, not executable member access.
evidence: CAS rer_1b74d5cc5e87f66649fe47319552a3eef74b1fd61e5bef1de313562f639137e0 found harness/pack-utils.mjs matched computed member access against loaderSource; switching to codeSource plus adapter_self_containment regression kept bun test, bun run proof, bun run packs:verify, and git diff --check passing.
record.application: For future lexical scanner hardening, bind broad token regexes to stripped executable source and add false-positive regressions for data literals before CAS closeout.

record.learning: When broad unsafe-loader syntax patterns scan transformed JavaScript, run them on literal-stripped executable source unless the pattern intentionally reasons about literal composition, because inert labels and regex payloads can otherwise reject valid packs.
evidence: CAS rer_ab4bfcbb35f25e5f7c72f8114aeaf77c2b33ebe50ac63d64414c02631ee93c43 found EVAL_PATTERNS still matched loader-looking string text after computed-member stripping moved to codeSource; moving EVAL_PATTERNS to codeSource plus literal regressions kept bun test, bun run proof, bun run packs:verify, and git diff --check passing.
record.application: For future scanner regexes, classify each pattern as executable-token, literal-composition, or import-grammar before choosing loaderSource versus codeSource.

record.learning: When validating sidecar commands, prefer classifying the entrypoint as a local artifact path before extension or artifact binding because package-scheme specifiers such as npm: or jsr: can share an executable suffix while resolving outside the pack.
evidence: CAS rer_5d86e81a53446d4f474535ae93b97e4c2e674bc4e5817aa501dfc28423dab5ba found deno run npm:pkg/mod.mjs could be artifact-bound by literal path; isLocalSidecarEntrypoint plus sidecar_security regression kept bun test, bun run proof, bun run packs:verify, and git diff --check passing.
record.application: For future sidecar runtime support, reject URL/package schemes before checking executable extensions or manifest artifact paths.

record.learning: When a JavaScript self-containment verifier scans code that may run under a different runtime than the scanner optimizer, scan a non-optimizing executable representation alongside transformed output because optimizer-erased annotations can hide runtime effects.
evidence: CAS review 019f3954-2cd9-7791-a786-269c03ac2b5d found a node sidecar with /* @__PURE__ */ process.exit(7) passed the Bun-transformed scan while Node still executed it; adding raw sidecar scan inputs and regressions kept bun test, bun run check, bun run packs:verify, and git diff --check passing.
record.application: For future sidecar or scanner changes, classify the runtime that executes each artifact and include raw-source regressions whenever transformed output is used for security checks.

record.learning: When a raw-source security scan processes TypeScript artifacts, prefer stripping type-only declarations before token regexes because TypeScript runtime erasure makes type-only import() and Function references non-executable.
evidence: CAS review rer_6e882ce312ab3695eb74ea3d52bd92052c0440a6688c68243d0d60547e0e1120 found Node/Deno .ts/.mts sidecar raw scans rejected type-only import("node:fs") and Function references; adding type-only stripping plus pass/fail regressions kept bun test, bun run check, bun run packs:verify, and git diff --check passing.
record.application: For future raw scanner changes, distinguish executable syntax from type-only syntax before applying host-global and dynamic-loader regexes.

record.learning: When a raw-source JavaScript security scan compensates for optimizer elision, prefer normalizing executable identifier escapes and consuming complete TypeScript type declarations before token checks.
evidence: CAS review rer_fc1c3406190c4d6933005d2e1b86e373a0f9864d33d4330e51ce1e4ed87f4931 found pro\u0063ess escaped past raw process checks and multiline type aliases left type-only Function/import() text behind; identifier normalization plus balanced type-alias stripping kept bun test, bun run check, bun run packs:verify, and git diff --check passing.
record.application: For future raw scanner paths, normalize executable code after stripping literals/comments/types, and test escaped identifiers plus multiline type-only declarations together.

record.learning: When a raw fallback security scan must catch optimizer-erased JavaScript in TypeScript artifacts, neutralize optimizer purity pragmas and run the established TypeScript transform instead of hand-stripping type syntax; this preserves runtime-only calls while erasing annotations, assertions, and type declarations.
evidence: CAS found a false positive where raw Node/Deno TypeScript sidecar scans flagged erased annotations such as function parameters typed as Function and 'as import("node:fs").Stats' assertions.
The fix replaced the custom type-only declaration stripper in harness/pack-utils.mjs with an optimizer-pragmas-neutralized transform and added a regression in test/adapter_self_containment.test.mjs.
record.application: For scanner fixes that compensate for optimizer elision, prefer transformable normalized source over ad hoc TypeScript grammar stripping; add both false-positive and optimizer-erasure regressions.

record.learning: When extensionless local import or require validation sees a same-name directory with package.json, prefer rejecting that package-backed directory even if a covered direct candidate exists because runtime-specific resolution can execute the directory package instead of the verifier's preferred artifact.
evidence: CAS review 019f39ab-b98c-7d02-8307-cd871b31b6a1 found a Node .cjs sidecar with require('./helper') could pass via covered helper.cjs while Node can load helper/package.json main, leaving unchecked code unscanned.
The fix made directory package.json rejection unconditional for extensionless/directory specifiers and added a Node CommonJS sidecar regression in test/adapter_self_containment.test.mjs.
record.application: For future import-resolution hardening, treat direct files and package-backed directories as separate runtime alternatives; do not let one covered candidate suppress validation of the other.

record.learning: When extensionless Node/CommonJS require validation models runtime alternatives, prefer explicitly rejecting native addon candidates such as .node and index.node because they are executable, non-scannable files that can be loaded before covered JavaScript candidates.
evidence: CAS review 019f39be-1d14-7ff0-9ddd-08ce2eb156c2 found require('./helper') can load helper.node or helper/index.node while the verifier only covered JS/TS/JSON candidates, allowing unchecked native code to bypass self-containment.
The fix added unsupported runtime import candidate checks for .node and regressions for direct helper.node and helper/index.node candidates in test/adapter_self_containment.test.mjs.
record.application: For future extensionless resolution changes, list both coverable candidates and explicitly rejected non-scannable runtime candidates for every target runtime.

record.learning: When security checks scan JavaScript artifacts transformed by an optimizing loader, prefer scanning an optimizer-resistant representation for every artifact because environment folding and purity elimination can erase forbidden runtime branches before regex-based checks run.
evidence: CAS review 019f39c8-c9f3-7931-bf43-863d37af4988 found process.env.NODE_ENV production branches containing Function('return process') were folded away under CI defaults before EVAL_PATTERNS and PROCESS_ACCESS ran.

The fix made loaderScanInputs always include an optimizer-resistant source, uses raw scans for plain JS, neutralizes optimizer inputs before transforming TS/JSX-family sources, and adds adapter plus TypeScript Node sidecar regressions.
record.application: For future scanner changes, make transformed output a convenience input only; bind security decisions to an optimizer-resistant path that still normalizes syntax enough to avoid type/JSX false positives.

record.learning: When a pack declares Node or Deno sidecar execution, prefer requiring explicit local import specifiers for sidecar and helper artifacts because Bun-style extension probing can accept code that the declared runtime cannot resolve.
evidence: CAS review 019f39d5-9963-7530-a09b-66b2f6586a7c found Node sidecars with import './helper' or require('./helper') could verify via helper.mjs/helper.cjs even though Node would fail to resolve those extensionless specifiers.
The fix rejects extensionless or directory local specifiers for non-Bun sidecar artifacts and adds Node CJS, Node ESM, and Deno sidecar regressions.
record.application: For future sidecar import resolution work, route candidate expansion through the declared runtime or require explicit specifiers instead of applying Bun candidate rules globally.

record.learning: When a computed-member scanner rejects constructed property access, prefer treating literal receivers such as strings, numbers, bigints, and regex literals as executable receivers because they can still expose constructed properties through bracket access.
evidence: CAS review 019f39d5-9963-7530-a09b-66b2f6586a7c found 'abc'[key], 0[key], and /x/[key] passed because previousSignificant saw quote/digit/slash instead of an identifier or closing delimiter.
The fix added literal receiver detection, taught regex-literal stripping about export default regex expressions, and added string, number, bigint, and regex receiver regressions.
record.application: For future scanner hardening, classify receiver syntax before excluding non-identifiers; preserve false-positive tests around array literals and division when adding new receiver forms.

record.learning: When extensionless runtime-candidate checks see a local specifier with an unsupported dotted suffix, treat it as runtime-probed rather than explicit because Node can still append .js, .json, or .node to names such as helper.v1.
evidence: CAS review 019f39e3-3cca-7141-a736-f601acbdce16 found require('./helper.v1') skipped helper.v1.node because hasExplicitExtension treated .v1 as explicit even though Node still probes native addon candidates.
The fix changed specifierUsesRuntimeResolution and unsupportedRuntimeImportCandidates to use hasSupportedImportExtension and added dotted native-addon plus non-Bun dotted sidecar regressions.
record.application: For future resolution checks, distinguish any dot from a supported runtime extension; unsupported suffixes still need candidate expansion or explicit rejection.

record.learning: When neutralizing optimizer-controlled environment constants before TS-family scanner transforms, prefer covering string-literal bracket property forms such as process['env'].NODE_ENV and process.env["NODE_ENV"] because Bun can fold them like dotted process.env.NODE_ENV.
evidence: CAS review 019f3a00-4491-78b1-b199-7d3ee4d5f79a found a Node/Deno .mts sidecar branch guarded by process['env'].NODE_ENV could be erased before security scans because only the dotted NODE_ENV form was rewritten.
The fix centralizes an OPTIMIZER_NODE_ENV_ACCESS pattern covering dotted and bracketed env/NODE_ENV forms and adds bracketed .mts sidecar regressions to the optimizer-folded environment branch test.
record.application: For future optimizer-resistance changes, enumerate semantically equivalent constant-property forms before transform and test them on non-plain artifacts that cannot be scanned raw without type-syntax false positives.

record.learning: When validating local import self-containment across runtimes, prefer rejecting percent-encoded dot path segments before candidate expansion because Node ESM can URL-decode specifiers such as ./%2e%2e/evil.mjs to paths outside the pack.
evidence: CAS review 019f3a0c-7ede-7a93-b9c9-1b505725e0f5 found a Node sidecar import of ./%2e%2e/evil.mjs passed verification as the covered in-pack path %2e%2e/evil.mjs but executed ../evil.mjs outside the pack.
The fix adds hasEncodedDotSegment before local import candidate expansion and a covered non-Bun sidecar regression for ./%2e%2e/evil.mjs.
record.application: For future runtime import resolution checks, normalize or reject URL-encoded path-control syntax at the specifier boundary before comparing checksum coverage candidates.

record.learning: When stripping JavaScript line comments for security scanning, prefer using the ECMAScript line terminator set because U+2028 and U+2029 end // comments even when optimizer-erased code would otherwise hide forbidden calls.
evidence: CAS review 019f3a28-e06c-7171-b127-53136dcef929 found Function('return process') after a // comment terminated by U+2028 passed after Bun erased the dead branch and skipLineComment treated the call as still commented.
The fix adds an isLineTerminator helper for CR, LF, U+2028, and U+2029 and a regression that writes both Unicode separators before a forbidden Function call in an optimizer-erased branch.
record.application: For future scanner comment handling, keep lexical terminator rules aligned with ECMAScript rather than ASCII-only newlines, especially on optimizer-resistant raw scans.

record.learning: When blocking Function-constructor recovery in scanner-based self-containment checks, prefer rejecting scope-rebinding constructs and plural descriptor APIs because with scopes and Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors can recover Function without dotted constructor access.
evidence: CAS review 019f3a38-de95-7da0-aaca-46387fa42d7c found a CJS with (function(){}.__proto__) block let bare constructor resolve to Function, and Object.values(Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors(function(){}.__proto__)) let a pack locate the Function descriptor while passing verification.
The fix rejects with statements, broadens getOwnPropertyDescriptor to getOwnPropertyDescriptors?, and adds CJS with-scope plus plural descriptor Function recovery regressions.
record.application: For future unsafe-loader scanning, include ambient scope recovery and API pluralization variants when extending constructor/prototype recovery deny patterns.

record.learning: When allowing Node TypeScript sidecars, prefer validating against Node's strip-only TypeScript subset before Bun-transformed scanning because Bun can compile syntax that Node refuses at runtime.
evidence: CAS review 019f3a43-6f64-7793-a3f7-ca37d11be6ba found a Node .mts sidecar with constructor(public x: number) passed verification after Bun transpilation but node sidecar.mts exits with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX.

The fix adds nodeSidecarRequiresStripOnlyTypeScript, rejects enum/namespace/module/parameter-property syntax for Node TS sidecar and helper artifacts, and adds parameter-property plus enum regressions.
record.application: For future sidecar runtime support, bind syntax acceptance to the declared runtime parser, not only the scanner transform used for analysis.

record.learning: When screening Node strip-only TypeScript syntax, prefer running deny rules on inert-text-stripped source with erased declare containers neutralized because raw regex checks can reject valid sidecars while still missing transform-only import-equals declarations.
evidence: CAS review 019f3a54-cae6-7660-8fd9-5f64a5ee22f9 found the first Node TS denylist rejected inert string/comment text and missed import-equals declarations that Node rejects in strip-only mode.

The fix runs the denylist over nodeStripOnlyTypeScriptSyntaxSource, neutralizes declare enum/namespace/module containers, rejects non-type import-equals, and adds positive inert/declare plus negative namespace/import-equals regressions.
record.application: For future runtime syntax gates, separate parser-valid erased TypeScript from transform-only runtime syntax, and run syntax deny rules on executable-looking source instead of raw text.

record.learning: When tracking template-literal expression depth for security scans, prefer skipping comments before counting braces because braces inside comments can truncate raw optimizer-resistant scans and hide executable loader calls.
evidence: CAS review 019f3a61-c2b0-7112-b1ad-b61f99655a29 found readTemplateExpression counted a } inside a line comment, so the optimizer-resistant scan lost a later PURE-marked Function/process call while the transformed scan erased it.

The fix skips line and block comments in readTemplateExpression before brace accounting and adds line-comment plus block-comment sidecar regressions for template expressions hiding optimizer-erased loaders.
record.application: For future scanner depth machines, handle comments, strings, regexes, and nested templates before structural delimiter accounting so inert delimiters cannot alter executable-source boundaries.

record.learning: When validating Node strip-only TypeScript sidecars, prefer including decorator syntax in the transform-only denylist because Node rejects decorators before startup even when Bun can parse or transform the file.
evidence: CAS review 019f3a7d-390b-7a63-aa8a-e0cb0a97d37e found a Node .mts/.cts sidecar containing a TypeScript decorator passed verifySelfContained but node sidecar.mts fails before startup with SyntaxError.
The fix adds a stripped-source decorator pattern to NODE_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX and extends the Node transform-only syntax regression table with a decorator case.
record.application: For future Node TypeScript runtime checks, treat decorators as runtime parser compatibility syntax rather than scanner-only syntax, and cover it alongside enums, namespaces, parameter properties, and import-equals.

record.learning: When distinguishing for-of syntax from computed member access, prefer requiring a real for or for-await head without a top-level initializer assignment because contextual identifiers named of can otherwise hide computed access in classic for initializers.
evidence: CAS review 019f3a8b-aa8b-79f0-8c22-fb01191da17b found for (let x = of[key](...); false;) was treated as a for-of head, letting computed Function/process recovery pass verification.

The fix reuses isForHeadPrefix for for/for-await, rejects head prefixes with top-level assignment before of, allows array binding pattern delimiters, and adds regressions for classic for initializer computed access, array binding patterns, and for-await RHS array literals.
record.application: For future scanner keyword heuristics, validate contextual keywords by their full syntactic head and separately model binding-pattern delimiters so false negatives and false positives do not trade places.
